images.title: Hidden common factor
images.purpose: Show that 56 and 63 are not co-prime because both have the factor 7.
images.composition: Two equal rows stacked with wide space between them.
images.exact_structure: Top row: 56 in a teal #0072B2 box, then 7 × 8 with the 7 filled reddish purple #CC79A7. Bottom row: 63 in an amber #E69F00 box, then 7 × 9 with the 7 filled reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 2 rows, 2 purple 7 boxes.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: One factorisation can hide a common factor, so look for more.
images.description: Two rows: 56 = 7 × 8 and 63 = 7 × 9 with both sevens highlighted, labelled 7 is common.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the 7 in each row.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
